gap: No result ChatGPT got says which max heights assume the centre column is raised. With the column down, the shortlist's tripods reach 127–133 cm, except the $109.90 budget pick Sirui Traveler 5C, whose 138 cm advertised height drops to 102.5 cm (a retailer figure). Its column makes up about a quarter of its height, against about 15% for the others.
standout_why: I compared against two rival pages. digitalnomads.world (cited) gives Peak Design at 152.4 cm and Ulanzi Zero Y at 156.7 cm without saying the column is up, and has no Sirui 5C or Befree Advanced entry. findingtheuniverse.com (cited) gives Peak Design at 60 in, says to keep the column down in wind, but gives no column-down height for any tripod. Neither page has column-down heights or compares them across models. On load ratings, findingtheuniverse already warns they aren't standardised and digitalnomads already splits the Ulanzi's 3 kg / 5 kg / 18 kg ratings, so the load point is only partly new. I could not read amateurphotographer.com (cited): it returned HTTP 403.
decides: This mostly confirms the upgrade tier and weakens the budget pick for adults. Peak Design, Ulanzi Zero Y and Manfrotto Befree Advanced all reach 127–133 cm with the column down, so their stable working heights are within about 6 cm of each other. The choice between them comes down to weight, packed size and price. The Sirui 5C reaches 102.5 cm without its column (retailer figure), about 25–30 cm lower than the others, so a standing adult must raise the thin column, which the reviewers advise against. The 5C suits short or seated setups. Anyone shooting at eye level outdoors should move up a tier.
